Sura 98: Al-Bayyina (The Clear Proof)

Meccan, though it is said to be Medinan. It has 8 verses. [It was revealed after Surat al-Talaq.]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

So God, exalted is He, related what they used to say, and then said: ﴿Those who were given the Book did not become divided except after the clear proof had come to them﴾. The meaning is that they used to expect that unity of word and agreement upon the truth would come with the coming of the Messenger; then, it was only the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) that divided them from the truth and did not leave them upon disbelief. The parallel to this in speech is that a poor sinner says to one who admonishes him: "I will not cease from what I am in until God grants me wealth." Then God grants him wealth and he increases in sinfulness, so his admonisher says: "You were not ceasing from sin until you became rich, and you did not plunge your head into sin except after you became affluent," reminding him of what he used to say, as a rebuke and a reproach.

The disengagement (infikak) of a thing from another is that it separates from it after being joined to it, like a bone when it comes out of its joint. The meaning is: they are firmly attached to their religion, not abandoning it except when the clear proof (al-bayyina) comes. Al-bayyina is the evident proof [[In a variant reading in place of "al-bayyina," the text reads: the Qur'an. ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the earlier scriptures, and a messenger from God﴾: Gabriel, peace be upon him, who recites the purified pages copied from the Preserved Tablet mentioned in Surat Abasa. A omitted noun must be supplied, namely "revelation." It is also permissible that what is meant is the Prophet (ﷺ). If you ask: how is the recitation of the purified pages attributed to him when he was unlettered? I answer: when he recites the like of what is mentioned in them, he is reciting them.... (Z)]]. "A messenger" is in apposition to "the clear proof." In the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "a messenger," as a circumstantial accusative (hal) from "the clear proof." ﴿Purified pages﴾, sheets of paper free from falsehood, ﴿in which are upright writings﴾, straight, speaking the truth and justice.

Nafi' read "al-bariyya" with a hamza, while the other readers read it without hamza. "Al-nabiyy" and "al-biriyya" are words whose usage has continued with their lightening, abandoning the original form. It is also read "khiyar al-bariyya," the plural of khayr, like jiyad and tiyab as plurals of jayyid and tayyib.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites [Surat al-Bayyina] will be on the Day of Resurrection with the best of creation, in the evening and in the morning." [Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

It is also read "wa dhalika al-din al-qayyima," interpreting "religion" as "community." If you ask: what is the sense of His words ﴿They were not commanded except to worship God﴾? I answer: the meaning is: they were not commanded by what is in the two books except in order that they worship God in this manner. Ibn Mas'ud read "illa an yabudu," meaning "that they worship." Nafi' read "al-bariyya" with a hamza, while the other readers read it without hamza. "Al-nabiyy" and "al-biriyya" are words whose usage has continued with their lightening, abandoning the original form. It is also read "khiyar al-bariyya," the plural of khayr, like jiyad and tiyab as plurals of jayyid and tayyib.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites [Surat al-Bayyina] will be on the Day of Resurrection with the best of creation, in the evening and in the morning." [Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

Sura 98: Al-Bayyina (The Clear Proof)

Meccan, though it is said to be Medinan. It has 8 verses. [It was revealed after Surat al-Talaq.]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The disbelievers of both groups, the People of the Book and the idolaters, used to say before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We will not cease from what we are upon of our religion, nor abandon it, until the promised Prophet comes, who is written of in the Torah and the Gospel, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ)." So God, exalted is He, related what they used to say, and then said: ﴿Those who were given the Book did not become divided except after the clear proof had come to them﴾. The meaning is that they used to expect that unity of word and agreement upon the truth would come with the coming of the Messenger; then, it was only the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) that divided them from the truth and did not leave them upon disbelief. The parallel to this in speech is that a poor sinner says to one who admonishes him: "I will not cease from what I am in until God grants me wealth." Then God grants him wealth and he increases in sinfulness, so his admonisher says: "You were not ceasing from sin until you became rich, and you did not plunge your head into sin except after you became affluent," reminding him of what he used to say, as a rebuke and a reproach.

The disengagement (infikak) of a thing from another is that it separates from it after being joined to it, like a bone when it comes out of its joint. The meaning is: they are firmly attached to their religion, not abandoning it except when the clear proof (al-bayyina) comes. Al-bayyina is the evident proof [[In a variant reading in place of "al-bayyina," the text reads: the Qur'an. ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the earlier scriptures, and a messenger from God﴾: Gabriel, peace be upon him, who recites the purified pages copied from the Preserved Tablet mentioned in Surat Abasa. A omitted noun must be supplied, namely "revelation." It is also permissible that what is meant is the Prophet (ﷺ). If you ask: how is the recitation of the purified pages attributed to him when he was unlettered? I answer: when he recites the like of what is mentioned in them, he is reciting them.... (Z)]]. "A messenger" is in apposition to "the clear proof." In the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "a messenger," as a circumstantial accusative (hal) from "the clear proof." ﴿Purified pages﴾, sheets of paper free from falsehood, ﴿in which are upright writings﴾, straight, speaking the truth and justice.

By their dividing is meant: their separating from the truth and their dispersal from it. Or it means that they split into factions: some of them believed, some of them denied and said, "He is not [the one]," and some recognized and obstinately rejected.
